newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SAS to lift prices due to higher fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: SAS to lift prices due to higher fuel costs.

text.p: Scandinavian airline SAS on Tuesday said it was increasing passenger ticket prices by 2.0 percent and freight price by 5.0 percent due to higher fuel costs.
"The sharp price increase on jet fuel in recent months forces SAS, like other airlines, to increase its ticket prices," the airline said in a statement.
It said SAS would raise its passenger fares in Scandinavia from November 15 to compensate for the unexpected cost developments.
"At the same time cargo prices will be increased by about five percent," SAS said.
It said fuel prices had increased by an average of 16 percent in 1996 compared to average prices in 1995.
"During the latest two months the increase has been even larger, with the price of jet fuel now nearly 40 percent higher than at the same time last year."
It said several airlines had already warned about price increases on their respective markets.
"The price increase by about two percent on the passenger side from November 15 applies to the airline's entire network, including domestic and international," SAS said
SAS said some of the increases on fares such as those to Asian countries were subject to local authorities.
"The increase in freight prices applies to the entire network," it said.
SAS is owned in part by the governments of Sweden, Denmark and Norway.
